analysis.investment_thesis: Desco Infratech is a recently-listed micro-cap infrastructure contractor with a derisory 0.26% ROE and no verifiable multi-year earnings record — it fails virtually every quantitative test I require. The 10.4x P/E is illusory given earnings power this thin, and there is no margin of safety for a disciplined investor.
key_strengths: P/E of 10.4x is below my 15x ceiling on reported figures
Promoter holding of 58.31% indicates skin in the game
Exposure to diversified infra verticals (CGD, renewables, water)
key_risks: ROE of 0.26% signals negligible earning power on deployed capital
Recently listed micro-cap (INR 124 Cr) — no long earnings track record to verify
Civil construction is working-capital heavy, cyclical, and prone to receivable losses
red_flags: ROE effectively zero — reported EPS likely a rounding artifact
Negligible institutional ownership (DII 2.2%, FII 0%) — no independent validation
Recent BSE SME-style listing; IPO pricing favors the seller, not the buyer
No disclosed dividend record, current ratio, or debt metrics
analysis.detailed_analysis:
An ROE of 0.26% is the most damning number in this dossier. It means that on whatever book equity supports this business, management is generating almost nothing for owners — a P/E of 10.4 on near-zero earnings is mathematically trivial and economically meaningless. Combined with a market capitalization of only INR 124 Cr and a recent BSE listing code (544387), this has every hallmark of the speculative small-issue offerings I warned against in Chapter 6 of The Intelligent Investor: the underwriter and promoter sell at the top of favorable market conditions while the public absorbs the risk.

I cannot verify the Graham Number, current ratio above 2.0, debt-to-equity under 0.5, or five consecutive years of adequate earnings from the data provided — and civil construction companies routinely fail the last three. Until Desco demonstrates at least five years of audited, stable earnings, a robust balance sheet, and a dividend record, it belongs in the speculative bucket, not the investment bucket. Mr. Market is offering a story here, not a bargain. Pass.
